question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $59u+16v=\text{gcd}(59,16).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}59 & = & 16\cdot 3 & + & 11 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 16 & = & 11\cdot 1 & + & 5 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 11 & = & 5\cdot 2 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(59,16)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}11 & =59-16\cdot 3 \\ 5 & =16-11 \\ 1 & =11-5\cdot 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =11-5\cdot 2 \\  & =11-(16-11)\cdot 2 \\  & =11\cdot 3-16\cdot 2 \\  & =[59-16\cdot 3]\cdot 3-16\cdot 2 \\  & =59\cdot 3-16\cdot 11 \\  & =59\cdot 3+16\cdot (-11)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=3$ and $v=-11.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=3+(-11)=-8.
$$
